full_judgment: 34. The learned Attorney-General submitted that fishery in this country is managed by the Government as Government khas property like other khas lands under the instruction as contained in the State Manual. The introductory chapter of the State Manual says that the State Manual deals with the principal policy and with the procedure for the management of the properties owned by the Government as khas or acquired by the Government under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. This Manual, according to the learned Attorney General consists of administrative directions having no statutory force. Further section 76 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act only authorises the Government to manage the Government fishery after its acquisition which is thus only a permissive law while the Fish Protection Ordinance, 1959 is prohibitory, prohibiting fishing in government fishery without a licence and though the said Ordinance speaks of a Rule to be framed for the purpose of giving effect to the provision of that Ordinance of 1959 no such Rules had yet been made as in the Madras Case referred to by the petitioner and thus those Ordinances are merely enabling laws without making any Rules for the purpose of giving effect to the provision of the Ordinance, only when a question of acting under statutory authority or Rules would arise.
